determinism.identity: Certificate content identity is lowercase SHA-256 of complete canonical serialized bytes, including verdict, observations, diagnostics, and non-semantic extensions, while certificate_id is a stable logical identifier
determinism.ordering: verification artifacts, trust dependencies, diagnostics, hashes, features, support references, dimensions, truncation IDs, and related references sort and deduplicate by their declared stable identity
determinism.replay: basis_sha256 covers certificate ID, subject, format, checker, complete Evidence header, and replay fields other than itself; deterministic mode forbids a seed and seeded mode requires one exact nonnegative seed
determinism.serialization: UTF-8 canonical JSON uses NFC strings, sorted mapping keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, bounded integers, no floats, and exactly one trailing newline

effects.filesystem: none during construction, validation, replay-identity calculation, serialization, or content identity calculation; Evidence and artifact bytes are supplied explicitly and are not opened implicitly
effects.mutation: constructed values are immutable and caller-owned mutable objects are never retained by alias
effects.process: none; resource, replay, and checker values report external execution but validation launches, signals, and terminates no process
effects.solver: none; checker observations are represented and validated without invoking a producer solver or verification backend

ensures: Certificate contains one stable logical ID, the exact Evidence subject and header, a versioned certificate format, independent checker identity, deterministic replay basis, checker-produced verification artifacts, explicit trust closure, one verification verdict, terminal resource snapshot, complete diagnostics, and namespaced non-semantic extensions.

Certificate is a checker observation rather than a producer artifact: verified authority is impossible without independently validated Evidence bytes, a distinct checker or external component, exact replay match, checker result, replay log, and complete trust dependencies.

The Evidence reference binds canonical Evidence SHA-256, logical ID, exact subject, primary payload hash, format ID and version, required feature set, dependency content hashes, and producer contract, implementation, configuration, role, and component identity.

Format version, numeric major and minor, minimum reader minor, schema identity, canonicalization algorithm, and required features agree exactly; unsupported major versions and version-confusion mutations fail closed.

Replay identity binds certificate ID, subject, format, checker, Evidence header, deterministic or explicitly seeded algorithm, configuration, expected payload, observed payload, and input Evidence identity before verdict interpretation.

Verified requires observed payload identity equal expected primary payload identity, checker-result and replay-log artifacts produced by the named checker, and authority matching checker versus external role.

Invalid, unsupported, inconclusive, cancelled, exhausted, truncated, verifier-failed, and disagreement verdicts remain explicit and can never be promoted to verified by payload labels, extension data, resource completion, or producer assertions.

Replay mismatch is represented as invalid only when a distinct observed payload hash differs from the expected hash; absent, interrupted, unsupported, inconclusive, failed, or truncated replay cannot become verified.
Cancellation, exhaustion, and truncation match the ResourceBudget terminal outcome exactly; all other verdicts require a completed resource ledger and cannot hide an interruption.

Canonical serialization and SHA-256 identity are reproducible without clock origin, process ID, checkout path, random values outside an explicit seed, implicit backend identity, or mutable caller state.

epistemics.cancelled: verification observed an identified cancellation and no successful replay or mathematical verdict is implied
epistemics.checker_attested: the named distinct checker component produced the verified observation under exact contract, implementation, configuration, environment, input, and replay identities
epistemics.disagreement: checker observations conflict across at least two retained artifacts and no verified authority is selected
epistemics.exhausted: one or more exact budget dimensions lacked capacity and partial checker work has no verified authority
epistemics.external_verified: the named distinct external component produced the verified observation under the same complete binding requirements
epistemics.inconclusive: the checker completed without a verified or invalid determination and retains its reason without truth authority
epistemics.invalid: one or more contract invariants fail and no Certificate content identity or epistemic authority is returned
epistemics.invalid_evidence: the checker completed and recorded a semantic, dependency, Evidence, or replay mismatch with checker-result evidence and a diagnostic
epistemics.mathematical_truth: authority remains conditional on explicitly named checker and trust dependencies and is never inferred from producer output, format names, structural validity, or resource completion alone
epistemics.truncated: one or more identified checker outputs were omitted under explicit ResourceBudget truncation and cannot support verification
epistemics.unsupported: the checker cannot interpret one or more explicit Evidence or certificate features and no verified authority exists
epistemics.valid: all representation, canonicalization, identity, Evidence binding, independence, replay, artifact, trust, verdict, diagnostic, outcome, and budget invariants pass without itself proving checker honesty or the mathematical claim
epistemics.verified: an independent checker or external verifier replayed exact Evidence under complete trust bindings, emitted checker-result and replay-log artifacts, and observed the expected payload identity
epistemics.verifier_failed: the checker process or semantic engine failed and the failure remains an error rather than a verified or invalid mathematical judgment

invariants: The normative schema is docs/contracts/schemas/certificate-v1.schema.json=cbc8f68469593e1d2b34588b49eaa16e37d597c863457945dd5b9ce5ae138760 and unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

Certificate, checker, replay-attempt, verification-artifact, and diagnostic IDs share one collision-free envelope namespace; artifacts, diagnostics, trust dependencies, set-valued hashes, features, support references, dimensions, and truncation IDs use their declared canonical order.

Certificate format major is exactly 1, semantic version major and minor equal numeric compatibility fields, minimum reader minor does not exceed writer minor, and feature identifiers are sorted reverse-DNS names.

The Evidence header equals the independently validated Evidence bytes field-for-field and binds exact content SHA-256, subject, primary payload, format compatibility, dependency content set, and producer provenance.

Checker component ID differs from producer component ID; checker role is checker or external; identical producer and checker contract-plus-implementation pairs fail closed even under different labels.

Deterministic replay has no seed, seeded replay has one exact nonnegative seed, replay configuration equals checker configuration, input and expected hashes equal the Evidence reference, and basis_sha256 matches the normative replay basis.

Every verification artifact is produced by the named checker, artifact IDs sort and deduplicate, kind-plus-content identities do not repeat, and all verdict and diagnostic artifact references resolve.
Verified authority matches checker role, support contains the named checker-result and at least one replay-log artifact, observed and expected payload hashes match exactly, and diagnostics are empty.

Verified trust closure contains exactly one checker contract, checker implementation, checker configuration, environment contract, ProblemIR, TheoryContext, and Evidence dependency with hashes matching the corresponding bound inputs.
Invalid replay_mismatch contains a non-null observed payload hash unequal to the expected hash; invalid always retains a checker-result artifact and diagnostic.

Every non-verified verdict retains a diagnostic; verifier failure and disagreement retain error severity; disagreement references at least two distinct checker artifacts; extensions cannot override inputs, replay, verdict, trust, budget, identity, or authority.
Cancelled, exhausted, and truncated verdicts match the budget outcome; verified, invalid, unsupported, inconclusive, verifier-failed, and disagreement require a completed budget outcome.

Canonical input contains at most 67108864 bytes, 4000000 visited values, 64 nesting levels, 100000 envelope entities and items per array, and 1048576 code points per string; validation is bounded by 30 seconds.

The complete canonical Certificate bytes, including verdict, observations, diagnostics, and non-semantic extensions, have one lowercase SHA-256 content identity while certificate_id remains a stable logical identifier.
raises: EvidenceCertificateValidationError with kind schema for unknown or missing fields, malformed tagged unions, invalid enums, duplicate JSON keys, invalid scalar types, or noncanonical extension values.
EvidenceCertificateValidationError with kind canonical, compatibility, identity, reference, epistemic, artifact, replay, diagnostic, outcome, or budget for the corresponding failed invariant.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit are never converted into verified, checker-attested, externally verified, valid, completed, or otherwise successful certificates.
requires: Input is a schema-exact mathhead.certificate.v1 object governed by docs/contracts/schemas/certificate-v1.schema.json=cbc8f68469593e1d2b34588b49eaa16e37d597c863457945dd5b9ce5ae138760.

The referenced Evidence is governed by accepted MH-C-EVIDENCE-001=c68c20ca599cfdd7aabe9b85f2817c6c3f1a121289334136ff048768ee20c3b3 and its complete canonical bytes are independently loaded, schema-validated, semantically validated, and SHA-256 checked before a verified verdict is permitted.

The checker has checker or external role, a component identity distinct from the Evidence producer, and exact contract, implementation, configuration, environment, name, and version bindings; its contract-plus-implementation identity differs from the producer pair.

Every verification artifact and trust dependency is content-addressed; consumers independently obtain and hash referenced bytes before assigning mathematical authority beyond structural contract validity.

All strings are Unicode NFC without NUL, JSON contains no floats, integers stay in the portable exact range, root extensions use reverse-DNS namespaces, nested extension keys use lowercase snake case, and declared hard ceilings are satisfied.
